name: Regia
description: A read-only control room for your Orca bots: what is waiting on you, the queue by priority, who is working on what, and how work flows between bots, workers and pull requests.

statusBarItems.tooltip: Regia: what is waiting on you

settings.title: Bot that holds the queue
settings.description: The name or id of the bot whose items are your queue, if one bot orchestrates the others. Leave empty to see the open items of every bot, grouped by bot.

settings.title: Read priority and project from item titles
settings.description: Reads titles written as “🔴 Project · what to do · ⏰ 24/12 17:00”: the dot is the priority (🔴 today, 🟠 within 3 days, 🟡 this week, ⚪ whenever), then the project, then an optional deadline as day/month and time. Any other title is shown as it is.

settings.title: Project order
settings.description: Project names separated by commas, in the order you want their lanes. Other projects follow in alphabetical order. Used only when one bot holds the queue.

settings.title: Animations
settings.description: “Follow the system” stops the animations when your system asks to reduce motion. “Off” stops them always.

settings.title: Notify when something new is waiting on you
settings.description: One desktop notification for each new question from a bot or an agent. The same one is never repeated.

settings.title: Slow refresh, in seconds
settings.description: The queue, agent states and messages are re-read every 4 seconds. Everything else (other items, workers, chats, automations) is re-read in turns, and this is how long a full turn takes. Between 10 and 300.

settings.title: Bots not there yet
settings.description: Names separated by commas, shown dashed until a bot with that name exists in Orca.

settings.title: State file (optional)
settings.description: Path to a JSON state file that adds model, effort, context, cache and file overlaps for each agent. Leave empty to keep this source off: no file is looked for or read.

settings.title: Orca CLI executable
settings.description: Leave empty to use Orca's own CLI, then `orca` on the PATH.
